visual_goal: Show SFP's intended boundary: the platform owns per-transaction facts and computes amounts; S/4HANA owns accounts, periods and balances and receives summaries it can drill back from; payments, tax and safeguarding are shared services the platform calls.
prompt: An illustration with a large central rounded teal panel labeled 'Stayloft Finance Platform'. Inside the panel, a tidy row of four small boxes: 'Commission rating', 'Subledgers', 'Payout engine', 'Summarization'. At the far left, a box labeled 'Booking platform' with one lightning-bolt arrow into the panel labeled 'events'. Above the panel, three small separate service boxes in a row on a soft grey strip labeled 'Shared services': 'Payments', 'Tax', 'Safeguarding'; each is connected to the panel by one double-headed arrow. At the far right, a large open book labeled 'S/4HANA general ledger'. Between 'Summarization' and the book: one thick arrow right labeled 'summaries', and below it one thin dashed arrow back left labeled 'drill-back'. Under the book a small row of three icons with labels 'Accounts', 'Periods', 'Balances'.
alt: The Stayloft Finance Platform with commission rating, subledgers, payouts and summarization receives booking events, calls shared payment, tax and safeguarding services, and sends summaries to the S/4HANA general ledger, which owns accounts, periods and balances and drills back into the platform.

visual_goal: Show summarization as safe only when reversible and provably complete: detail is summarized with batch IDs, posted to the GL, drill-back via the batch index returns to detail, and a daily reconciliation compares both sides and sends breaks to an exception queue.
prompt: A loop illustration. At the top left, a tall stack of many thin paper slips labeled 'Detail lines'. One arrow right through a funnel labeled 'Summarize' into a small neat stack of documents with tag icons labeled 'Batch summaries'. One arrow right from the summaries into an open book labeled 'General ledger'. One dashed arrow from the book down and back left labeled 'drill-back' into a card index box labeled 'Batch index', and one arrow from the index box up into 'Detail lines', closing the loop. Below the loop sits a balance scale labeled 'Daily reconciliation', with one arrow into it from 'Detail lines' and one arrow into it from 'General ledger'. From the scale one small red arrow down into a tray labeled 'Exception queue'.
alt: Detail lines are summarized into batch summaries posted to the general ledger; drill-back through the batch index returns to the detail lines, and a daily reconciliation weighs detail against the ledger, sending breaks to an exception queue.

visual_goal: Show the per-component retirement test: differentiation decides whether convergence is considered; a proven alternative, a full cost comparison and a preserved audit trail decide whether it happens now.
prompt: A left-to-right path of four diamond checkpoints in a row connected by green arrows: 'Differentiates?', 'Platform proven?', 'Cheaper to converge?', 'Audit trail kept?'. After the last diamond a green arrow leads to a box with a calendar icon labeled 'Converge on a plan'. Above the first diamond, one arrow goes up to a box with a shield labeled 'Keep custom'. Below the second and third diamonds sits one wide box with an hourglass labeled 'Tolerate and retest', spanning under both diamonds; one arrow drops from 'Platform proven?' into it and one arrow drops from 'Cheaper to converge?' into it, both arrowheads touching the box. Below the fourth diamond, one arrow down into a box with an archive-box icon labeled 'Build archive first'.
alt: Four checks in a row: does it differentiate, is a platform proven, is converging cheaper, can the audit trail be kept; passing all leads to converging on a plan, otherwise keep custom, tolerate and retest, or build the archive first.
